title: Model attrition trigger matrix and response scenarios
creator: Priya Nair
description: Scope: define a repeatable, prioritized signal-to-action matrix for model attrition (when a model becomes unsuitable for Redwood customers due to capability regression, license changes, cost/latency regression, region availability, or security/compliance flags). Goal is to reduce time-to-mitigation from signal detection to customer-safe fallback to under 48 hours for P0/P1 signals and provide a 30/60/90 plan for model replacement where needed. This ticket covers research, signal taxonomy, tooling requirements, initial dashboard prototype, executive decision rules, and a communications/runbook template for account teams and support.
acceptance_criteria: Signal taxonomy documented and reviewed by Applied ML and Security
Decision matrix with clear actions for each severity level (auto-fallback, staggered rollout, customer outreach) published in Confluence
Prototype dashboard in Console for top 20 models showing live attrition signals and suggested actions
Automation backlog items created for ENG to implement the top 3 signal detectors
Runbook and customer communication templates approved by GTM and Legal
deliverables: Console dashboard prototype URL and mockups
CSV mapping of alternative model variants with integration effort estimates and cost delta
Runbook: P0/P1/P2 response procedures and communication templates
signal_definitions: Quality drift: sustained negative eval delta vs baseline across control prompt set (>5% F1 degradation over 7 days)
Latency delta: 95th pct latency increase >30% sustained for 24 hours
Cost delta: per-token cost increase due to model change or quantization issues >25% for a sustained period
License change: vendor announces license/alignment change affecting allowed use (detected via vendor feed)
Availability/regional deprecation: model endpoints removed in a region or capacity pages indicate removal
Security/compliance flag: new vulnerability, CVE, or failed compliance audit
decision_matrix: P0 (security/vulnerability): immediate global automatic fallback to vetted variant + pager + legal escalation
P1 (severe quality/regression): automatic routing to previous verified model for requests from affected customers; create urgent model-repro-run and notify affected customers within 24 hours
P2 (cost/latency increases): apply regional routing to cheaper variants and schedule optimization sprint; notify customers on Dedicated plans if their SLA affected
P3 (minor drift/noisy signal): continue increased sampling and scheduled eval; trigger canary run of model variant replacement
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize taxonomy with Applied ML and Security, create Confluence pages, agree on severity thresholds
Week 2: small engineering spike to surface signals into internal metrics pipeline (alerts prototype), build dashboard mockups with Console PM
Week 3: implement auto-routing rules for one critical variant, author runbook templates, legal review of customer comms
Week 4: iterate on detection thresholds using historical telemetry, onboard first 10 customers for test alerts
risks_and_mitigations: False positives causing unnecessary failovers: mitigate with conservative thresholds and two-stage confirmation (metric + sample eval)
Latency of signal ingestion delaying response: prioritize implementation of lightweight detectors in telemetry pipeline first
Customer confusion or panic from communications: coordinate GTM/Support to use templated messaging with clear remediation steps
Dependency on vendor-supplied feed for license changes: add manual monitoring and legal contact points as backup
